newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aminex in deal to tap Russian Tatarstan oil fields.
newsitem.headline: Aminex in deal to tap Russian Tatarstan oil fields.

text.p: Aminex Plc of Ireland has signed a production-sharing deal with four Russian energy firms to tap oil reserves in Russia's autonomous republic of Tatarstan, a Russian company official involved in the deal said on Wednesday.
Yuri Agababov, a deputy general director at Zarubezhneft, one of the Russian firms which is part of the deal, said an agreement had been signed but did not give further details.

Other companies involved in the deal were AO Tatneft (an independent oil company with about six percent of Russia's total proven crude oil reserves and based in the central region of Tatarstan) and two affiliated units -- Tatnefteprom and Tatneftekhiminvest-Holding.
Interfax news agency said the deal with Aminex would focus on hard-to-recover reserves containing up to 40 million tonnes of crude oil. No other details were immediately available.
Tatneft's oil output, excluding joint venture production, slipped last year to 23.70 million tonnes (474,000 barrels per day) from 24.14 million tonnes (482,800 bpd) in 1995.
The company issued level-one American Depositary Receipts in July 1996 and plans a Eurobond by the end of this year.
